name: Gaal
overview: Gaal is a male figure known primarily as the son of Ebed, who was trusted by the men of Shechem. His identity is closely linked to this trust within the community of Shechem, as recorded in Judges 9:26. There is no additional information about his tribal affiliation or other distinguishing notes.
namesAndTitles: The name Gaal is a proper name meaning 'loathing.' It was not given by God but is recorded in Judges 9:26. This meaning may reflect aspects of his character or role within the narrative, though the text does not elaborate further.
familyAndRelationships: Gaal is explicitly identified as the son of Ebed, according to Judges 9:26. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not record additional family connections for Gaal.
scriptureSignificance: Gaal's significance in the biblical narrative arises from his relationship to Ebed and the trust placed in his family by the men of Shechem. This trust situates him within the political and social dynamics of Shechem during the period described in Judges. His presence underscores the local leadership and alliances that played a role in the unfolding events of that time.
